title: ScVal map whose keys U32(1) and Symbol("1") collide when converted to native keys (js-stellar-sdk#1789)
why: The two keys are distinct ScVals in host order, so a contract can return or emit this map. Converting it to a native object keyed by text makes both keys "1": a converter that does not refuse silently drops one entry.

source.reason: A bare ScVal built by hand from the XDR definitions (the js-stellar-sdk#1789 value); a contract can return or emit it, but these bytes were not taken from core output

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: scValToNative returns an object with 1 key(s) and no error. 17.3.0 and later throw 'scvMap has more than one key that converts to …'. Earlier 17.x versions were not run.
known_divergences.evidence: evidence/js-1789/transcript-prefix.txt (17.2.1) and transcript-fixed.txt (17.3.0); xcc conform run --columns 'js@17.2.*' --entries 'cap-0046/scval-map-keys-collide-u32-symbol'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: scValToNative returns an object with 1 key(s) and no error; the fix of the v17 line was not backported to v16.
known_divergences.evidence: xcc conform run --columns 'js@16.*' --entries 'cap-0046/scval-map-keys-collide-u32-symbol' (L3 ok, native.map_entries 1 of 2 on each version)

notes: The value of js-stellar-sdk#1789, hand-encoded from the XDR definitions (evidence/js-1789/). stellar-core 30.0.0 print-xdr --filetype scval decodes it to the same two entries (run by hand for this entry).
